name: Shimo-Kitazawa
tagline: Shibuya in 8 minutes and Shinjuku in 11 minutes. Served by 2 lines.
summary: The station is in Setagaya City, served by Keio Inokashira Line and Odakyu Odawara Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 29 minutes to Otemachi, 11 minutes to Shinjuku, 8 minutes to Shibuya and 34 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 36.5 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 12.6 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 36.5 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 29.5 m to 42.1 m, a difference of 12.6 m. These figures were read from the elevation API of the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan at nine points: the station itself and eight compass directions 400 m out.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 4 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.

groceries.name: オオゼキ 下北沢店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 15 clinics and 10 pharmacies. Facilities recorded as hospitals lie at 加藤医院, about 144 m away and 島津メディカルクリニック, about 210 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Keio Inokashira Line and Odakyu Odawara Line. The lines are split between operators (Keio runs 1 line and Odakyu runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company. Scored out of 100 from the number of lines and the spread of operators, transfer convenience here comes to 52.
